title: Vector RAG
text: Vector retrieval-augmented generation splits documents into chunks, turns each chunk into a dense embedding, and answers a question by pulling the nearest chunks in embedding space into the prompt. It works well when the answer sits inside one passage, but it struggles with multi-hop questions whose answer is spread across several documents, because each chunk is scored in isolation.

title: GraphRAG
text: GraphRAG builds a knowledge graph of entities and the relationships between them from the source corpus, then groups related entities into communities with generated summaries. At query time it can walk relationships to connect facts that live in different documents, which makes it stronger than chunk-only retrieval for global and multi-hop questions.

title: BM25 lexical ranking
text: BM25 is a lexical ranking function that scores a document by how often the query terms appear in it, weighted by inverse document frequency and normalised for document length. Because it matches exact tokens, it is excellent for error codes, product SKUs, part numbers and rare names that embedding models tend to blur together.

title: Hybrid search
text: Hybrid search combines a lexical score such as BM25 with a dense semantic score from an embedding model. The two lists are merged either with a weighted sum of normalised scores or with reciprocal rank fusion, so the final ranking benefits from exact keyword matches and from paraphrase understanding at the same time.

title: Cross-encoder reranking
text: A cross-encoder reranker is a second-stage model that reads the query and a candidate passage together in one forward pass and outputs a relevance score. It is far more accurate than comparing two independent embeddings but also much slower, so it is only applied to the top few dozen candidates returned by a cheaper first-stage retriever.

title: Chunking strategy
text: Before indexing, long documents are split into smaller windows, usually with some overlap so a sentence cut at a boundary still appears whole in one window. Small windows give precise matches but lose context; large windows keep context but dilute the embedding. Typical sizes range from a few hundred to about a thousand characters.

title: LangGraph
text: LangGraph models an agent as a stateful graph: nodes are functions that read and update a shared state, and edges, including conditional edges, decide what runs next. It supports cycles for research loops, persistent checkpointing so a run can resume after a crash, and human-in-the-loop interrupts, which gives fine-grained control in production.

title: CrewAI
text: CrewAI organises agents as a crew of role-playing members, each with a role, a goal and a backstory, that collaborate on a list of tasks. It is quick to prototype with and reads naturally, but it hides much of the control flow, so debugging, deterministic routing and fine-grained retries are harder than in lower-level orchestration frameworks.

title: Operating agents in production
text: Running LLM agents in production means tracing every step, capping token spend, retrying flaky tool calls with backoff, and keeping the workflow deterministic enough to debug. Teams usually add structured logs, per-run cost reporting and timeouts around each external call.

title: Snowflake data cloud
text: Snowflake separates storage from compute. Compute runs in virtual warehouses that can be resized or suspended independently and are billed per second while running. Features such as zero-copy cloning and time travel make it easy to create test environments and recover earlier versions of a table.

title: Databricks lakehouse
text: Databricks is a lakehouse platform built on Apache Spark. Data is stored in open Delta Lake tables on cloud object storage, which adds ACID transactions to a data lake. It is strong for machine learning and large-scale data engineering, and Unity Catalog provides governance across workspaces.

title: Google BigQuery
text: BigQuery is Google Cloud's serverless data warehouse. There are no clusters to manage; with on-demand pricing you pay for the number of bytes each query scans, while capacity pricing reserves slots. Partitioning and clustering tables reduces the data scanned and therefore the cost.

title: Migrating an on-premise warehouse
text: Moving an on-premise warehouse such as Teradata or Netezza to the cloud usually follows five steps: assess workloads and dependencies, convert schemas and stored procedures, transfer historical data, validate results by running old and new systems in parallel, and finally cut over and decommission the legacy hardware.

title: Neo4j
text: Neo4j is a property graph database. Data is stored as nodes and relationships, both of which can carry key-value properties, and it is queried with Cypher, a declarative pattern-matching language where arrows describe the relationships to traverse.

title: Qdrant
text: Qdrant is an open-source vector database written in Rust. It stores embeddings together with a JSON payload and can filter on payload fields, for example a tenant or investigation id, during the similarity search rather than after it.

title: HNSW index
text: Hierarchical Navigable Small World is an approximate nearest neighbour index. It builds a layered proximity graph where upper layers hold few long-range links and lower layers hold many short links, so a search can jump quickly towards the region of the query and then refine locally.

title: Citation verification
text: Language models sometimes state facts with confidence and attach sources that do not actually support them. A citation verification pass checks every claim in a generated answer against the text of the source it cites and flags or removes claims that are unsupported, which reduces hallucinated evidence.

title: Contradiction detection
text: When evidence comes from many sources, some of it will conflict. Contradiction detection compares pairs of claims about the same entity, often with a natural language inference model or an LLM judge, and records which sources disagree so the final report can present both sides.

title: Dense embeddings
text: Embedding models such as bge-small map text to dense vectors so that passages with similar meaning land close together, measured by cosine similarity. This lets retrieval match paraphrases and synonyms even when the query and the passage share no words.

title: SSRF protection
text: Server-side request forgery happens when an attacker makes a server fetch a URL of their choosing, such as a cloud metadata endpoint or an internal admin page. Defences include resolving the hostname and refusing private, loopback and link-local IP ranges before any request is sent.

title: Model Context Protocol
text: The Model Context Protocol is an open standard that lets an application expose tools, resources and prompts to AI clients. A single MCP server can be plugged into Claude Desktop, Cursor or any other compatible client without writing a separate integration for each one.

title: LLM knowledge extraction
text: To build a knowledge graph from raw text, an LLM is prompted to extract entities and the claims or relations between them as structured triples of subject, predicate and object. The triples are then deduplicated and merged into graph nodes and edges.

title: Shortest paths in graph theory
text: In graph theory, Dijkstra's algorithm finds the shortest path from one node to every other node in a graph with non-negative edge weights by repeatedly expanding the closest unvisited node using a priority queue.

title: Snowflake schema in dimensional modelling
text: In dimensional modelling, a snowflake schema normalises dimension tables into several related tables, whereas a star schema keeps each dimension in a single denormalised table joined directly to the fact table. Star schemas need fewer joins; snowflake schemas reduce redundancy.

title: Data lakes versus data warehouses
text: A data warehouse stores cleaned, structured data in a schema designed for analytics, while a data lake stores raw files of any format cheaply on object storage. Many teams now combine the two so that one copy of data serves both BI dashboards and machine learning.
